notes: Maps every N02 invariant to the golden scenarios that exercise it (crates/franken-control/tests/vectors/n02_scenarios.json) and to the Rust tests under crates/franken-control/src/channel that check it.

tests/n02/test_reference_model.py verifies the mapping: each scenario names only declared invariants, each invariant has at least one scenario, each listed Rust test exists, and docs/contracts/n02.md mentions each invariant.
Everything here is host simulation of a message-handling state machine. It says nothing about a network, a real MAC, a board or an audible result.

invariants.claim: A request that does not authenticate changes nothing: no queue, no ledger entry, no rate-limit allowance.
When the acknowledgement of a committed command is lost, the retry is answered with the recorded outcome and the command is not applied again.
However many times a command is delivered, it takes effect at most once.
A duplicated relative volume change applies exactly one delta, whether the copy arrives before or after the original is applied.
A storm of retries leaves queue length and ledger size unchanged and produces one effect.
The same command number with different content is refused, while the first is waiting and after it settled.
After the retention period an outcome is forgotten, and a retry is answered as unknown (never re-applied).
When the ledger is full the oldest outcome is forgotten explicitly, and newer ones are still answered.
Exactly-once is not promised forever: beyond the window the channel reports unknown and does not guess.
A controller acting under an old epoch changes nothing once the group's epoch has moved on.
A key bound to one epoch is refused at the door under any other epoch.
Nothing the channel applies can advance the group's epoch, so a request cannot fence out the legitimate leader.
A command whose expected revision is not the current one is refused with no effect.
A peer revoked or rebound after its command was accepted has no effect when the command would run.
Every queue is bounded; a full lane refuses new work, and a refusal for want of room does not consume the command number.
A request turned away before acceptance can be sent again unchanged once the reason has passed.
A command refused after acceptance has its refusal recorded as its outcome, and a retry is told the same.
Rate limits are per authenticated peer and per lane, and refusals state the exact wait.
Stop, mute and cancel travel in a separate lane that is served before ordinary work.
A local stop is applied in the first step after it is accepted, ahead of every queued remote command, through a full queue and a remote flood.
The local user keeps priority slots a remote peer cannot take, and the lane is still bounded.
Priority never bypasses authentication: a forged stop is refused like any forged request.
The local user is not refused for epoch or expected revision; a remote controller in the same position is.
An accepted command that waits longer than the pending limit expires unapplied, and that is its recorded outcome.
No retry or wait is unbounded: queue time, ledger memory and rate are all limited.
Cancel withdraws a waiting ordinary command of the same peer before it commits, and changes nothing after, for another peer, or against a stop.
Relative volume is resolved against the live value in the channel and clamped to 0..=100.
A step applies at most its budget of commands; the rest wait for the next step.

A session refusal that is not about the command's content (a repeated or out-of-window number, a stale epoch) is an internal fault: counted, kept for the operator, recorded without detail and never shown to the sender. An unknown member is still the sender's.
After a channel restart against a session that kept running, a copy composed before the restart is refused whatever its kind, nothing is reverted, and a command composed after the restart is applied.
A restarted channel numbers its session commands above everything its predecessor used, so the first commands after a restart are not session faults.

Absolute volume stays naturally repeatable: a command composed against an older revision than the current one still applies within an incarnation, so pipelined updates and interleaved controllers are not stale.
A remote controller's volume or mute command must name the revision it last read, or it is turned away at the door without consuming its number; stop, cancel and the local user need none.
A command naming a revision the session has not reached is refused with no effect.

A command that changes the group is applied only under a live group lease (a G01 AuthorityToken the session still accepts at the time of the step); with none, a superseded one or an expired one it is refused before the session is touched.
After the issuer advances the epoch, a late command under the old lease is refused, and the same command is applied once the new epoch's lease is installed.
A lease is live up to the instant before its expiry and refused from that instant; renewal plus resubmit is applied.
A lease the session does not accept (foreign issuer or group, stale, future, already expired) cannot be installed, and the lease already held keeps working.
A refusal for want of a live lease is reported but not recorded, so the same request sent again after the lease is installed or renewed is judged afresh.
A local stop and a local mute-on only silence and need no lease; a cancel only withdraws its sender's waiting work and needs none.
A forged request fails authentication before the lease is consulted.
Every command that reaches a terminal outcome in a step is written to the log exactly once, with its correlation id, the committed revision, the epoch, the queue depth and the time it waited.

invariants.claim: With a clock-uncertainty margin u the held lease stops being usable u before its expiry, exactly where G01's own liveness rule stops it; a lease with no more than u left cannot be installed.

A holder whose lease is about to expire renews it through a quorum win and keeps applying commands with no gap; a lapsed holder's renewal is refused and its commands stay refused until it wins a new epoch; a newer holder's adoption fences the old lease; a renewal needs a held lease and a quorum group and cannot be replayed to stretch the lease.
invariants.scenario_inapplicable: Renewal needs G01's real quorum machinery (voters, rounds, wins), which the Python model does not model; the Rust tests drive G01's own LeaseVoter, QuorumRound and GroupMembership.

invariants.claim: An on-time acknowledgement completes its ledger entry exactly once, a second is a duplicate, and acknowledging does not change how long an outcome is remembered.

invariants.claim: A revocation survives a restart if the owner stores the tombstone snapshot and restores it into a fresh directory first: the stale admission of a revoked identity is refused at or below its tombstone, the key is answered Revoked exactly as before the restart, a deliberate re-admission one version up works, a malformed snapshot is refused whole, and a restart that forgets, mis-versions or restores a stale snapshot lets the revoked key back or leaves it refused for the wrong reason (the judge catches each by name).
invariants.scenario_inapplicable: The Python scenario model has no restart or persistence operation; the Rust tests judge it through the channel, with planted persistence faults.

invariants.claim: After a full process restart, a stored revision high-water mark restored before the first step raises the revision floor to at least the mark: a held-back copy composed against the old history is refused exactly as StaleRevision even after the rebuilt session climbs past its revision, a fresh command composed against the restored session is admitted, the local user is never affected, and a mark is accepted only before the first step; a restart that stores nothing or a stale mark admits the copy, one that overshoots locks fresh controllers out, and the judge catches each by name.
invariants.scenario_inapplicable: The Python scenario model has no process restart or persisted mark; the Rust tests judge it through the channel with planted persistence faults.

invariants.claim: The channel's production source uses no thread, lock, atomic, Arc, clock read, file, socket, process, environment or unsafe, and under a six-thousand-operation flood every structure it keeps stays within its cap after every operation; the per-peer tables are bounded by the authority's identity cap, and an authority that admits every identity takes them past their caps and the census catches it.
invariants.scenario_inapplicable: These are properties of the source text and of the structures' sizes under load, judged by Rust tests that read the channel's own files; the Python scenario model has nothing to say about either.

invariants.claim: The revision high-water mark is stored on U01's journal after each step and read back at boot: after a process death, only the durable bytes survive, a held-back copy is refused exactly as StaleRevision, a fresh command applies and the journal then holds the new mark; an owner that never restores, and one whose first process never stored, admit the copy and the judge catches each by name.
invariants.scenario_inapplicable: These are properties of the channel over U01's journal on an in-memory medium with fault injection, judged by Rust tests; the Python scenario model has no journal and nothing to say about either.

invariants.claim: step_then_store returns a step's outcomes only after the mark that covers them is durable, and withholds them if the store fails; with the power cut at every storage operation and byte budget of one store the recovered mark is exactly the old or the new one, and the duplicate of every delivered command is refused; an owner that delivers before it stores is caught by the sweep, and one that forgot to restore cannot store over the mark.
invariants.scenario_inapplicable: These are properties of the channel over U01's journal on an in-memory medium with fault injection, judged by Rust tests; the Python scenario model has no journal and nothing to say about either.

invariants.claim: A journal that cannot be read (opening fails, or neither segment is valid) gives the channel the floor u64::MAX instead of the session's revision: for that run every remote command that names a revision is refused as StaleRevision, the local user still commits, and the floor is never stored; an owner that treats the unreadable journal as no mark admits the copy and the judge catches it by name.
invariants.scenario_inapplicable: These are properties of the channel over U01's journal on an in-memory medium with fault injection, judged by Rust tests; the Python scenario model has no journal and nothing to say about either.

invariants.claim: A reply is accepted only if its tag is HMAC-SHA256 under the peer's key with the reply label over its signed bytes: a forged tag (all zero, made under the request context, the request's own proof, another peer's key) and any change to one signed field of a genuine reply are refused as bad_tag, checked first.
invariants.scenario_inapplicable: A reply is a wire format and a client check, and the Python scenario model has no wire to put it on. The independent evidence is tests/n02/gen_reply_vectors.py (hand-written layout and results, a separately written decoder and verifier) and tests/n02/test_reply_vectors.py (broken implementations caught by name), not a scenario.
